xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4338: Handoffs, forks and workers refuse a project's primary checkout as cwd

plan.title: Handoffs, forks and workers refuse a project's primary checkout as cwd
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: validateCwdContainment (src/lib/overdeck/conversation-forks.ts:172, twin in conversation-runtime.ts:224) accepts any existing directory under $HOME, including a registered project's primary checkout, so `pan handoff --cwd <primary>` / `pan fork --cwd <primary>` start agents that commit straight onto main (the 2026-07-01 incident in sync-sources/rules/handoff-isolate-cwd.md). pan worker run confines --cwd to the issue workspace but follows symlinks, so a symlinked member repo can still resolve to a primary checkout.
narratives.Proposal: Add a leaf resolver findPrimaryCheckout (src/lib/projects/primary-checkout.ts) that matches a path's canonical form or git top level against every registered project root and polyrepo member root. Collapse the two validateCwdContainment copies into src/lib/overdeck/cwd-containment.ts (semantics unchanged). The fork route refuses an explicit cwd that is a primary checkout with `Invalid cwd: <path> is the primary checkout of <project>; use a worktree` unless allowPrimary is sent by an operator (callerKind 'operator' or absent). The CLI (`pan fork`, `pan handoff`) gains --allow-primary and always sends callerKind from verdictCallerFromEnv, as `pan review restart` does. startWorker refuses a read-write --cwd that resolves to a primary checkout. Rule, skills and reference docs state the refusal. Full detail: .pan/drafts/pan-4338.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Refusing the inherited cwd (source conversation cwd, issue workspace, process.cwd()) when the request sends no explicit cwd
- Refusing resume or model/harness switch of an existing conversation (conversation-runtime.ts:393 and :1131 keep containment-only validation)
- Adding any primary-checkout logic inside the shared validateCwdContainment helper
- Checking POST /api/conversations (new conversation creation) or pan lane start
- Any dashboard frontend change (the Fork modal sends no cwd)
- A security boundary against a process that sends raw HTTP to the fork route without callerKind (this is accident prevention)
- An allowPrimary override for workers
- Git hooks or shims that block commits in the primary checkout (#4337 / deft-adoption issue 3)
- Editing src/lib/projects.ts

autoDecisions.summary: The refusal applies only to the fork route's explicit `cwd` body field and to a read-write worker's explicit --cwd, never to the inherited cwd.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator conversations such as conv-flywheel live in the primary checkout by design and the rule tells agents to run pan handoff from the project dir; refusing the inherited cwd would break every `pan handoff self` from them and the existing 'keeps the parent cwd' test. The issue's AC names the request cwd.

autoDecisions.summary: Collapse the two validateCwdContainment copies into one helper, but add the primary check only at the fork route, not inside the helper.
autoDecisions.rationale: conversation-runtime.ts calls it at :393 (model/harness switch) and :1131 (resume) on an existing conversation's cwd; refusing there would make every primary-checkout conversation impossible to resume. The issue title scopes the refusal to handoffs, forks and workers.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Primary checkout' = the canonical path OR its git top level equals a registered project root or polyrepo member root; non-git paths fall back to plain equality.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plain equality leaves `--cwd <root>/src` open, and commits from there land on the primary checkout just the same. Nested worktrees (workspaces/feature-*) have their own git top level and still pass.

autoDecisions.summary: The resolver is a new leaf module src/lib/projects/primary-checkout.ts exporting findPrimaryCheckout (returns the match or null), not isPrimaryCheckout in src/lib/projects.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: projects.ts is at its file-size allowlist ceiling (1217); path-containment.ts is the existing sibling for path helpers; the error message needs the matched project, so the function returns the match rather than a boolean.

autoDecisions.summary: allowPrimary is honored only when callerKind is 'operator' or absent (dashboard UI); the CLI always sends callerKind from verdictCallerFromEnv and sends allowPrimary only with the new --allow-primary flag on pan fork / pan handoff.
autoDecisions.rationale: Copies the existing `pan review restart` (#3853) pattern the issue points to. It stops agents that go through the CLI; it is documented as accident prevention, not a boundary against raw HTTP.

autoDecisions.summary: Workers get no override; read-only workers are not checked.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says 'apply the same check in pan worker run when not --read-only' and names no override; the read-only git guard already blocks commits.
useConversationMutations.ts summaryForkConversation sends no cwd, so the dashboard can never hit the refusal.

items.title: Add findPrimaryCheckout resolver in src/lib/projects/primary-checkout.ts

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-1 exactly. New file src/lib/projects/primary-checkout.ts exporting `PrimaryCheckoutMatch { projectKey; repoName: string | null; root }`, `PrimaryCheckoutDeps { listProjects?; gitToplevel? }`, `findPrimaryCheckout(path, deps = {})` and `primaryCheckoutLabel(match)` (returns `key` or `key/repoName`). Algorithm: candidates = canonicalPathAsync(path) plus canonicalPathAsync(gitToplevel(canonical)) when non-null (default gitToplevel = promisified execFile `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with cwd, null on error). For each project from listProjectsAsync with a path: root = canonicalPathAsync(config.path); match root → {key, null, root}; then each workspace.repos[] member: canonicalPathAsync(resolve(root, repo.path)) → {key, repo.name, memberRoot}. Else null. Async only (no *Sync, no execSync). Do not edit src/lib/projects.ts. Tests with real temp dirs and real git, injected listProjects: root, subdirectory, nested `git worktree add` (null), unrelated (null), polyrepo member (label 'poly/api'), symlink, non-git fallback via injected gitToplevel returning null.

items.title: Given a registered root or any subdirectory of it, findPrimaryCheckout returns { projectKey, repoName: null } (subdirectory matched through its git top level)
Given a git worktree added under <root>/workspaces/feature-x, or an unrelated directory, findPrimaryCheckout returns null
Given a polyrepo project whose workspace.repos has { name: 'api', path: 'api' }, the member root returns repoName 'api' and primaryCheckoutLabel returns 'poly/api'
Given a symlink to a registered root, or a non-git root with gitToplevel injected to return null, findPrimaryCheckout still returns the match

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-3 in handleConversationSummaryFork, directly after the `if (cwd && !(await validateCwdContainment(cwd)))` check (currently :826) and before createConversation: when cwd is set, `const primary = await findPrimaryCheckout(cwd)`; operatorOverride = body.allowPrimary === true && (body.callerKind === undefined || body.callerKind === 'operator'); if primary && !operatorOverride return 400 `{ error: `Invalid cwd: ${cwd} is the primary checkout of ${primaryCheckoutLabel(primary)}; use a worktree` }`. Import from '../projects/primary-checkout.js'. Only the explicit cwd is checked; the inherited effectiveCwd is not. Tests: vi.mock '../../projects/primary-checkout.js' with importOriginal + a vi.hoisted primaryRoot so findPrimaryCheckout returns { projectKey: 'demo', repoName: null, root } when the path equals primaryRoot (a dir under testHome); do not mock listProjectsAsync. Cases: summary fork refused + no new row (listConversations().length unchanged); handoff mode refused; worktree <primaryRoot>/workspaces/feature-pan-1 accepted with conversation.cwd equal to it; allowPrimary + callerKind 'agent' → 400; allowPrimary + callerKind 'operator' → 200; allowPrimary without callerKind → 200. Also add a case where the mock reports parentCwd as a primary checkout and the request sends no cwd: the route returns 200 and the new conversation's cwd equals parentCwd (D1: the inherited cwd is never refused). Existing 'keeps the parent cwd' test stays green.

items.title: Given cwd equal to a registered project root, the fork route returns 400 with error containing 'is the primary checkout of demo; use a worktree' in summary and handoff modes and creates no conversation row
Given cwd equal to a worktree of that project (<root>/workspaces/feature-pan-1), the fork route returns 200 and the new conversation's cwd equals that worktree
Given allowPrimary: true with callerKind 'agent', the route still returns 400; with callerKind 'operator' or no callerKind it returns 200
Given no explicit cwd and a source conversation whose cwd the resolver reports as a primary checkout, the fork route returns 200 and the new conversation's cwd equals the parent cwd
Add --allow-primary to pan fork and pan handoff; fork-client always sends callerKind

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-4. fork-client.ts: add `allowPrimary?: boolean` and `callerKind?: 'operator' | 'agent'` to ForkViaServerOptions; in forkConversationViaServer set `body['callerKind'] = opts.callerKind ?? verdictCallerFromEnv(process.env, readAncestorAgentIds).kind` and `if (opts.allowPrimary) body['allowPrimary'] = true` (import from '../../lib/cloister/verdict-caller.js'). handoff.ts and fork.ts: add allowPrimary to their options interfaces and pass it to forkConversationViaServer. src/cli/index.ts: add `.option('--allow-primary', 'Operator only: allow --cwd to be a project\'s primary checkout (refused for agent sessions)')` after the --cwd option of both `fork` (:377) and `handoff` (:387). Then `npm run build:cli && npm run generate:slash-commands` and commit packages/contracts/src/composer-commands.generated.ts. New test fork-client.test.ts stubs globalThis.fetch (first call returns { conversation: { id: 1, name: 'n', tmuxSession: 't', forkStatus: null } }, polls return the same) and passes { pollMs: 0, timeoutMs: 50 } or uses fake timers — never real multi-second waits.

metadata.sizeJustification: One cohesive guard defined item-by-item by the issue: 7 small items touching ~20 files, half of them tests and docs. The subsystem count is inflated by docs surfaces (sync-sources rule + two skills, docs/, reference/) and the generated CLI manifest in packages/contracts; splitting the docs or the CLI flag into sibling issues would ship a server refusal whose documented override does not exist yet.
